$comment: ⛔ THE CROSS-LANGUAGE PARITY FIXTURE FOR THE `kb/Work/` FRONTMATTER READER (kb/Work PB875, PB245).
The work register is read by TWO engines that cannot share code: `scripts/spec/work.py` (Python — `check`,
`next`, the ledger, the Phase-B dossiers) and `tests/_shared/WorkRegister.cs` (C# — the drift gates that
enforce `inventory_rows` and `closes_rows`). They read ONE file format, and for months they read it
differently: a list WRAPPED across two lines — the normal YAML shape, carried by kb/Work/PB205 for months —
was truncated by the Python reader and DISCARDED ENTIRELY by the C# one, so kb/Work/PB390 went on claiming
four inventory rows in the register while the gate that enforces claims saw none. `work.py check` called the
same note well-formed. Only the permissive reader was ever run by hand.
This file is what makes 'the two readers agree' falsifiable rather than a sentence in a commit message —
the same device `derivation-parity-cases.json` is for §1.1 (kb/Work PB315).
Each case is a raw frontmatter TEXT plus the NORMALIZED view both engines must produce. Absent and empty are
deliberately one answer (a missing key says exactly as much as an empty one); a MALFORMED value is a third
answer and carries an error CODE, because collapsing it into 'empty' is the fail-open PB875 is about.
Python: `python scripts/spec/work.py parity` (add --json for the C# gate to consume).
⚙ ADD A SHAPE HERE THE MOMENT THE REGISTER GROWS ONE. A shape neither engine is measured on is a shape they
are free to disagree about, and the disagreement is invisible until a note happens to use it.
